concerns.text: The 'exposure content' from which predictors are derived is never operationally defined. Reddit data records only what a user posted, not what they were exposed to; the plan's per-user aggregation (Task 2) yields the user's OWN comments, yet Tasks 5-6 derive authenticity_score/engagement_proxy 'from exposure content'. If exposure content = subreddits the user participates in, the predictor stream is a function of the user's own commenting choices — a self-selection confound the covariate set (Task 8) does not address. Specify the operational definition of a user's exposure set and acknowledge/model self-selection.

exposure_level is 'proportion of community comment volume in target subreddits within a 30-day window' computed from subreddit metadata. As defined, this is a subreddit-level constant: all users in the same subreddit mix receive the same value, and per-user variation arises only via which subreddits the user visits — i.e., again self-selection. The plan does not state how per-user exposure variation is generated, nor are 'target subreddits' ever defined/selected. Without this, the exposure × feature interactions may be near-degenerate or purely artifacts of user subreddit choice.

Construct validity: a 'vulnerability-marker lexicon' (e.g., 'I'm struggling', 'feeling low') is used to measure 'authenticity cues' of idealized self-presentation. Vulnerability markers are not a validated proxy for authenticity/idealization; the research question concerns idealized self-presentation features. The plan should either justify this construct mapping or add a validation step (e.g., face-validity check against a labeled sample) beyond the acknowledged-limitation note in research.md.

The a priori power check is described only as 'f² = 0.15, α = 0.05, power = 0.80' with a log if N < 500. It does not state the test it powers (which interaction, numerator df, number of predictors in Model 3) nor what action follows an underpowered result beyond logging. Name the specific test and the decision rule.

The spec's sole input is 'public Reddit comment datasets from Pushshift' (US-1, FR-011, Assumption 1), but no verified Reddit/Pushshift dataset exists in this round. The plan correctly refuses to fabricate a source and installs a Data Availability Gate, but the underlying spec requirement is unsatisfiable as written — the spec needs a verified, reachable Reddit dataset (or a revised data-source story) before FR-011/FR-013/SC-001 can be met with real data. Root cause is in the spec, not the plan.

FR-017 requires demographic proxies 'extracted from user profile metadata (e.g., Reddit "about" fields)'. Plan Task 9 says 'Demographic proxies (age/gender keyword patterns) from user text' — comment text, not profile metadata. The ingestion design (Task 2) drops author fields and aggregates comments only, so profile metadata is never ingested. Either the plan must ingest profile metadata or the spec's FR-017 wording must be revised to match the comment-text proxy; as written the plan does not implement FR-017's stated source.

The project's sole required input — public Reddit comment data with subreddit, body, created_utc, and per-user identifiers — has no verified source in this round. The plan's Data Availability Gate is the correct, honest handling (no fabrication, no inappropriate substitution), but as written the pipeline cannot produce any real results: every downstream task (T2–T21) executes only against synthetic fixtures. A verified, appropriate Reddit-comments dataset (correct modality: comment text + per-user history, not e.g. submission-only or structural dumps) must be identified and cited before this plan can be executed as research rather than as code-with-fixtures. The gate should additionally specify the acceptance criteria a candidate source must meet (fields, per-user linkage, license permitting redistribution of derived aggregates) so the next round can resolve rather than re-flag the block.

Spec's sole input ('public Reddit comment datasets from Pushshift', spec.md Assumption 1 / US-1) has no verified source, so the plan's Data Availability Gate halts all data tasks and no FR-001..FR-018 result can ever be produced as planned. The plan is internally honest about this, but plan and spec are fundamentally incompatible: either the spec must be revised to name a verifiable source, or a verified Reddit dataset must be supplied. As written, the plan cannot satisfy any success criterion (SC-001..SC-007) that depends on real data.

concerns.location: plan.md:Phase 1, Task 8 vs spec.md:FR-018 / Constitution VI
concerns.text: Plan covariates 'baseline_sentiment' and 'total_comment_count' are derived from the user's OWN comments (per contracts/processed_features.schema.yaml descriptions) yet enter Model 1 as regression predictors. FR-018 states 'preventing any feature derived from the user's own comments from being used as a predictor', and baseline_sentiment is computed nearly identically to the outcome self_eval_score (VADER sentiment), creating exactly the circularity Principle VI prohibits. Plan, data-model, and spec must be reconciled: either drop/redefine these covariates from non-own-comment sources, or the spec must explicitly exempt control covariates.

quickstart.md step 8 writes 'reports/sensitivity_summary.csv', but data-model.md's artifact table does not list this file (nor does any plan task name it — Task 21 says 'report effect-size variation' without a target path). Add the artifact to data-model.md and name the output path in plan Task 21.

FR-017 requires demographic proxies from 'user profile metadata (e.g., Reddit "about" fields)'; plan Task 9 derives them from 'user text' (comment content). These are different sources with different PII/coverage implications. Align the plan (and the ingestion schema, which currently drops author metadata at PII scrub) with the spec's stated source, or amend the spec.

The covariate `baseline_sentiment` is derived from the user's OWN comments and is entered as a predictor in Model 1 (Phase 3 Task 15). This directly violates FR-018/Constitution VI ('preventing any feature derived from the user's own comments from being used as a predictor') and creates partial circularity with `self_eval_score` (both are VADER sentiment of the same user's comments — baseline_sentiment is essentially a component of the outcome). Either drop it or derive a genuinely separate baseline (e.g., pre-window sentiment from a distinct time period).

`exposure_level` is defined as a community-level proportion (subreddit aggregate activity), yet the regression is fit at the user level with plain OLS. A subreddit-level predictor applied to user-level outcomes (a) has no within-subreddit variation, (b) requires clustered/robust standard errors or a multilevel model, and (c) 'target subreddits' are never operationally defined — no selection criterion exists anywhere in the plan. Specify the subreddit-selection rule and the dependence structure (clustered SEs by subreddit or mixed model).

Identifying 'the content a user is exposed to' requires knowing which subreddits the user visits — operationally, the user's own comment locations. So all three 'exposure-stream' predictors are conditioned on the user's own behavior, partially conflating predictor and outcome streams despite the claimed Principle VI separation. The plan should acknowledge this exposure-identification circularity as a limitation and state precisely how exposure content is assigned to a user (e.g., subreddits posted in vs. subscribed vs. all of Reddit).

FR-017 requires demographic proxies from user PROFILE METADATA ('about' fields); Task 9 derives them from user TEXT. Pushshift comment dumps typically lack profile metadata — either state the data field used or acknowledge the deviation from the spec's stated source.
